q: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by _____ covalent bonds.
e: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by three covalent bonds. An N2 molecule holds two nitrogen atoms with a triple covalent bond, which is why nitrogen is so unreactive. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms. Three is the word this version is asking about.

q: Nitrogen is a colourless, odourless gas and is very _____.
e: Nitrogen is a colourless, odourless gas and is very unreactive. Nitrogen gas is very unreactive because of the strong triple bond in N2.

q: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of _____.
e: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of -196℃. Nitrogen has a very low boiling point, which is why it is a gas at room temperature and is separated from liquid air. -196℃ is the word this version is asking about.

q: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of _____ percentage of nitrogen.
e: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of 78 percentage of nitrogen. About 78 percent of clean dry air is nitrogen. Clean dry air is about 78 percent nitrogen by volume. The mixture of gases around Earth is the atmosphere, and that mixture exerts pressure.

q: Nitrogen can be found in some fairly rare minerals such as _____.
e: Nitrogen can be found in some fairly rare minerals such as Chile saltpetre. Saltpetre and similar nitrate minerals are uncommon natural sources of combined nitrogen.

q: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by _____ of liquid air.
e: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by fractional distillation of liquid air. Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen, oxygen and argon by boiling point. Industrial nitrogen is taken from liquid air by fractional distillation.

q: In the preparation of nitrogen from the air, carbon dioxide is removed by passing the air through _____.
e: In the preparation of nitrogen from the air, carbon dioxide is removed by passing the air through caustic soda solution. Carbon dioxide is removed by passing the air through caustic soda solution.

q: In the preparation of nitrogen from the air, heated copper absorbs oxygen to form _____.
e: In the preparation of nitrogen from the air, heated copper absorbs oxygen to form copper(II) oxide. Listen for copper(II) oxide in that sentence.

q: Since nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, it is collected by the _____.

q: If nitrogen is required dry, it may be passed through a U-tube containing glass beads wetted with _____.

q: Since nitrogen has 5 electrons in its outermost shell, the oxidation numbers of nitrogen vary from _____ to +5.
e: Since nitrogen has 5 electrons in its outermost shell, the oxidation numbers of nitrogen vary from -3 to +5. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Nitrogen has five outer electrons, so its oxidation numbers run from -3 to +5.

q: The oxidation number of nitrogen in $N_2O$ is _____.
e: The oxidation number of nitrogen in N_2O is +1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.
